title: Hardcoded AWS-format access key committed to source
detail: Line 13 declares `const metricsToken = "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"`. The value matches the AWS IAM access key ID pattern (`AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}`). Committing credentials in source permanently embeds them in the version history and exposes them to every reader of the repository. Even if this specific value is a documentation placeholder, the pattern teaches callers to supply a real key in the same position, making future accidental commits likely. The token has no callers visible in this file.

title: TLS certificate verification disabled in HTTP client (InsecureSkipVerify: true)
detail: `newClient()` at lines 15–20 constructs an `http.Client` whose `TLSClientConfig` sets `InsecureSkipVerify: true`. This suppresses all certificate validation — expired, self-signed, or fraudulent certificates are silently accepted. Any caller using this client is therefore susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks that can intercept or alter traffic, including any token or credential it carries.

title: OS command injection via exec.Command("sh","-c",...) with unsanitised instance parameter
detail: `Console()` constructs a shell command at line 24 using `fmt.Sprintf("virsh console %s", instance)` and executes it through `exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...)`. Because the command is interpreted by a shell, any shell metacharacter in `instance` (e.g. `;`, `|`, `$(...)`, `` ` ``) allows execution of arbitrary commands with the process's privileges. `instance` is a caller-supplied function parameter with no sanitisation visible in this file.
